sections.h2: How is property tax handled in Campbell County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Campbell County has three offices that touch your bill: the Property Valuation Administrator sets the assessed value, the Sheriff's Office mails and collects the bill, and the County Clerk takes over delinquent bills. The PVA's own page says it does not set rates and does not collect money, and that each taxing district's board calculates its own rate from the assessments in its district.

The county sits in Northern Kentucky along the Ohio and Licking Rivers, and it has two seats of government, Newport and Alexandria. Sheriff's Office windows are in both. With 93,076 residents counted in 2020 and 615 people per square mile, Campbell is by far the densest of the four counties in this series, and its homes carry the highest values.

The PVA must assess at 100 percent of fair market value, the price a willing buyer and willing seller would agree on. Field representatives physically review every parcel at least once every four years, and new construction gets its own review.

sections.h2: When are Campbell County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Campbell bills usually go out around November 1, and the PVA's calendar says tax bills are delivered to the sheriff by September 15. In 2025 the sheriff ran the 2% discount phase from November 1 through November 30, which the PVA's calendar describes as payment with discount before December 1.

  • December 1 to December 31: pay the face amount.
  • January 1 to January 31: bills are delinquent, with a 5 percent penalty.
  • After January 31: 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff's add-on fee.
  • Prior-year taxes: paid at the County Clerk, not the sheriff.

One detail catches sellers off guard. The 911 fee on a Campbell County bill is not discounted, so a bill paid in the discount phase still shows the fee at full price. The sheriff sends the bill only to the owner of record, and cannot send it to a mortgage company, so owners with escrow should forward the bill right away.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Campbell County tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay online, by mail, or at either sheriff's location. The Newport office is in the County Administration Building at 1098 Monmouth Street and the Alexandria office is at 8330 West Main Street, both open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., per the sheriff's tax page.

Online payment runs through a vendor site. Credit and debit cards carry a 3 percent fee paid by the cardholder, e-checks carry a $3 fee, and e-checks are not accepted above $30,000. The sheriff says it receives no part of those fees. By mail, make the check payable to the sheriff and write the bill number on it, and your canceled check serves as the receipt.

If a check bounces, the bill returns to unpaid status on the sheriff's and PVA's records, and the repayment must follow the schedule on the bill. Keep that in mind in a closing week, when a pending check can leave a lien open.

sections.h2: What does the Campbell County appeal process look like?
sections.html:
You must speak with the PVA before the end of the 13-day inspection period, then file your appeal with the county. The PVA's calendar says the tax roll opens for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, and the Board of Assessment Appeals meets for five days beginning 25 to 35 days after inspection closes.

The state's calendar page gives the filing deadline as the workday after inspection ends, while the PVA's own calendar lists a window of six work days. Because the two differ, read the dates on your assessment notice and ask the PVA for the exact last day before you file. Compensated representatives at these hearings must be attorneys, appraisers, accountants, licensed brokers or similar professionals under KRS 133.120.

Strong evidence for a Newport or Alexandria house is a list of recent sales of similar homes, photos of damage, and repair estimates. The Department of Revenue says the PVA should be able to hand over the sales used to value your home, so ask for that list first.

sections.h2: How do Campbell County exemptions and corrections work?
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older, and owners who are totally disabled, can apply for the homestead or disability exemption, and the application is filed with the PVA, which can give you the cutoff for the year. The state says disability verification is due before December 31. The sheriff's page tells owners who turn 65 during the year to contact the PVA before paying.

The PVA at 1098 Monmouth Street, phone (859) 292-3871, is also the place to fix a wrong address, mailing address or owner name on a bill. The return stub on the bill can be used to report corrections, and the sheriff forwards them. Only the PVA can change an assessment or exemption.

Farm acreage is valued at its agricultural value, which the state's assessment guide says can sit far below the market price per acre in urban areas. A seller with a few acres at the edge of Alexandria should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

sections.h2: What happens to Campbell County taxes if I sell my house?
sections.html:
Taxes follow the property, so the title company will ask for a payoff of the current bill and any delinquent certificate before closing. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and the delinquency lien continues under KRS 134.420 no matter who owns the house afterward.

If a bill goes unpaid past the sheriff's season, it moves to the County Clerk with a 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's fee and 1 percent monthly interest. The clerk, county attorney and any third-party purchaser can then add fees, which the state's collection page works through in five payment examples, from about $1,388 to $1,704 on a $1,000 bill. Call the clerk at (859) 292-3845 for a current amount.

A seller who has fallen behind can still sell as-is. The payoff is taken out of the proceeds, so the sooner you get numbers from the clerk, the sooner you know what is left.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Campbell County homes?
sections.html:
Campbell County has the strongest housing market of the four counties covered here, with a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied value of $252,000 and 182 building permits issued in 2025. The county belongs to the Cincinnati metropolitan area, and Northern Kentucky University is in Highland Heights.

Owners of older Newport homes, rental duplexes or inherited houses can sell directly for cash if repairs or tenants make a standard listing slow.

faqs.q: When is Campbell County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed around November 1. The 2% discount ran November 1 through November 30 in 2025, December is the face amount, January adds a 5% penalty, and after January 31 a 10% penalty and sheriff's fee apply.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Campbell County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Sheriff's Office in Newport (1098 Monmouth Street) or Alexandria (8330 West Main Street), by mail, or online through the vendor link on the sheriff's tax page.

faqs.q: Does the 2 percent discount apply to the 911 fee?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff states that the 911 fee on a Campbell County bill is not subject to the 2% discount.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Campbell County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the PVA at (859) 292-3871. The sheriff only collects the tax and cannot change an assessment, address or exemption.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Campbell County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent bills sit with the County Clerk, and the payoff comes out of the sale proceeds at closing. Call the clerk at (859) 292-3845 to get the amount before you set a date.
